chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (peace be upon them) who said:
The woman whose husband dies, is maintained from his wealth.

key_terms.يُنْفَقُ: Maintenance is provided / spending is allocated

ai.seo_question: Who pays for a widow's maintenance if her husband dies during the waiting period?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a divorced woman whose husband dies during her waiting period (iddah) retains her right to maintenance (nafaqah) from his estate, a ruling derived from the principle that the marital bond remains partially intact until the iddah concludes. Shia jurists utilize this narration to distinguish between the financial obligations of a widow versus a divorced woman, emphasizing that the husband's wealth covers her sustenance during this transitional phase. This ruling underscores the continuity of financial responsibility in Shia fiqh even after the pronouncement of divorce but prior to the finalization of the separation.
